The Respondents are the distribution licensees, transmission licensees and power departments, mainly the beneficiaries of the Northern Region, which are procuring transmission services from the Petitioner. 5. The Petitioner has served a copy of the Petition on the Respondents, and notices of the filing of this Petition have been published in the newspapers in accordance with Section 64 of the Electricity Act, 2003 (hereinafter referred to as “the Act”). No comments or suggestions have been received from the general public in response to the notices published in the newspapers by the Petitioner. None of the Respondents have filed their replies to the Petition. 7. This order is issued considering the submissions made by the Petitioner vide affidavits dated 1.5.2025 and 12.2.2026. Having heard the representative of the Petitioner and perused the material available on record, we proceed to dispose of the Petition. better planning and the expeditious execution of the works. However, it is evident from submitted that the shutdowns were approved only intermittently and during off-peak solar generation hours, resulting in very limited working periods for completion of the works. Accordingly, the delay of more than 151 days (corresponding to about 1208 working hours) was attributable to the non-availability of the requisite shutdowns at the Bhadla Substation. The Petitioner has further submitted that the delay was beyond the Petitioner's control and that the events leading to it were unforeseen. It is further submitted that, although the constraints in availing the shutdowns could have led to a much greater delay, the Petitioner, through its experience and expertise in project planning and execution, curtailed the delay by making efficient and sustained efforts. The Petitioner has, therefore, prayed for condonation of the delay in completing the transmission asset, on the ground that the reasons were beyond the Petitioner's control. 46. We have considered the Petitioner's submissions. The Petitioner is entitled to reimbursement of the fee paid for filing the Petition and publication expenses incurred on this count, directly from the beneficiaries or the long-term customers, as the case may be, in terms of Regulation 94(1) of the 2024 Tariff Regulations. 96. We have considered the Petitioner’s submissions and perused Regulation 99 of the 2024 Tariff Regulations. In view of the explicit provision made under Regulation 99 of the 2024 Tariff Regulations, we permit the Petitioner, i.e., PGCIL, to bear the fees and charges of CTUIL and recover the same as additional O&M Expenses through a separate Petition until such regulation is notified and issued by the Commission. 109.
